questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride is warmed with CuCN/KCN. The organic product is:
questions.explain: Sandmeyer cyanation replaces –N₂⁺ by –CN, giving C₆H₅CN and N₂; benzoic acid needs a separate hydrolysis step.

questions.q: Which aryl halide is NOT normally prepared by the Sandmeyer reaction?
questions.explain: Copper fluorides do not work, so fluorobenzene is made by the Balz–Schiemann route (HBF₄, then heat).

questions.q: Which statement about the mechanism of the Sandmeyer reaction is correct?
options: Cu(I) transfers an electron to the diazonium ion, which loses N₂ to give an aryl radical
It is a simple SN1 loss of N₂ giving an aryl cation
Cu(I) is consumed and not regenerated
questions.explain: The reaction is a radical-nucleophilic aromatic substitution; the aryl radical takes X from Cu(II), regenerating Cu(I), and biaryl by-products support this route.

questions.q: How do the Sandmeyer and Gattermann reactions differ in the preparation of chlorobenzene from benzenediazonium chloride?
options: Sandmeyer uses KCl; Gattermann uses CuCl
Sandmeyer uses CuCl/HCl; Gattermann uses Cu powder with HCl, and Sandmeyer gives the better yield
Sandmeyer uses Cu powder; Gattermann uses CuCl, and Gattermann gives the better yield
questions.explain: The Sandmeyer reaction uses a copper(I) salt, the Gattermann reaction copper powder with the halogen acid; NCERT states the Sandmeyer yield is better.
